answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity expensive to fake: to join, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove fraud. Like a canyon that only lets one river through, the registry narrows entry to identities with something to lose, while a cedar grows slowly, so reputation accrues only through verified work over time and a fresh fake cannot borrow trust. Each claim carries a cipher signature tied to that stake, so creating a thousand Sybils means posting a thousand deposits, and the cost scales faster than the attack gains.
